record.paper_title: Whitehead's Asphericity Question and Its Relation to Other Open Problems
record.context_brief: Topological extension of the L2-Betti hypothesis
record.original_question: Suppose X is a finite 2-complex with a retract subcomplex V such that the quotient X/V is contractible. Is the first L2-Betti number of pi_1(X) at most the first L2-Betti number of pi_1(V)?

evidence.quote: Hypothesis 1.5 Suppose that X is a finite 2-complex, with retract a subcomplex V such that X/V is contractible. Then β1(2) (π1 (X )) ≤ β1(2) (π1 (V )) .

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a finite connected 2-dimensional CW-complex and let $V \subseteq X$ be a subcomplex which is a retract of $X$ (i.e., there exists a cellular map $r: X \to V$ with $r|_V = \mathrm{id}_V$) such that the quotient space $X/V$ is contractible. For a discrete group $G$, let $\beta_1^{(2)}(G)$ denote the first $L^2$-Betti number of $G$, defined as the von Neumann dimension $\dim_{\mathcal{N}(G)} H_1^{(2)}(EG; \mathcal{N}(G))$ of the first $L^2$-homology of a model for $EG$ with coefficients in the group von Neumann algebra $\mathcal{N}(G)$. Prove or disprove: under the above hypotheses,
$$\beta_1^{(2)}(\pi_1(X)) \;\le\; \beta_1^{(2)}(\pi_1(V)).$$
artifact.status_search_result: The hypothesis is stated as an open conjecture in the context of L2-methods applied to Whitehead's asphericity question. Searches reveal no resolution of this specific inequality; the surrounding Whitehead asphericity question itself remains open in general, and the L2-Betti number formulation is part of an ongoing program connecting it to other open problems (Kervaire–Laudenbach, Bass trace conjecture, etc.).

status_evidence.title: Whitehead's Asphericity Question and Its Relation to Other Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: L2-methods are brought to bear on the question and relate it to other open problems including Kervaire–Laudenbach and Bass trace.
status_evidence.claim: The L2-Betti hypothesis is presented as an open question linked to Whitehead's asphericity.

status_evidence.title: A Review of Whitehead's Asphericity Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Whitehead's 1941 question on subcomplexes of aspherical 2-complexes remains open in general.
status_evidence.claim: Whitehead's asphericity question is still open, supporting that this related hypothesis is also unresolved.
